paras.text: Raw materials for petrochemical industries are methane, ethane, propane and butanes. These are obtained primarily from natural gas processing plants. Gas oil and naphtha are obtained from petroleum refineries. Benzene, toluene and xylene are also primarily obtained from petroleum refineries.

paras.text: Chemical Industry refers to the industry, which is involved in the business of making different products from raw materials through chemical reactions. Chemical sector plays a fundamental role in economic development of any nation. It converts the essential raw materials into more than seventy thousand variety products for industry as well as the goods of consumers that people depend upon their daily lives.
paras.urdu: کیمیائی صنعت سے مراد وہ صنعت ہے جو کیمیائی تعاملات کے ذریعے خام مال سے مختلف مصنوعات بنانے کے کاروبار میں شامل ہے۔ کیمیائی شعبہ کسی بھی قوم کی معاشی ترقی میں بنیادی کردار ادا کرتا ہے۔ یہ ضروری خام مال کو صنعت کے لیے ستر ہزار سے زیادہ اقسام کی مصنوعات اور ان صارفی اشیا میں بدلتا ہے جن پر لوگ اپنی روزمرہ زندگی میں انحصار کرتے ہیں۔

paras.text: 22.3 Dyes
paras.urdu: 22.3 رنگ (ڈائز)

paras.text: Dyes are substances that are used to impart colour to various substrates, which adds value to products for their cost, including paper, leather, fur, hair, drugs, cosmetics, waxes, greases, plastics and textile materials.
paras.urdu: رنگ وہ مادے ہیں جو مختلف سطحوں کو رنگ دینے کے لیے استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جو مصنوعات کی قیمت میں اضافہ کرتے ہیں، جن میں کاغذ، چمڑا، سمور، بال، ادویات، کاسمیٹکس، موم، گریس، پلاسٹک اور کپڑے کے مادے شامل ہیں۔

paras.text: A dye is a coloured compound, normally used in solution, which is capable of being fixed to a fabric.

paras.pashto: رنګ یو رنګه مرکب دی چې معمولاً په محلول کې کارېږي او پر ټوکر د ټینګېدو وړتیا لري.

paras.text: The dye has a colour due to the presence of chromophore and its fixed property is due to the acidic or basic groups such as –OH, –SO₃H, –NH₂, –NR₂, etc.
paras.urdu: رنگ کا رنگ کروموفور کی موجودگی کی وجہ سے ہے اور اس کی پکا ہونے کی خصوصیت –OH، –SO₃H، –NH₂، –NR₂ وغیرہ جیسے تیزابی یا اساسی گروپوں کی وجہ سے ہے۔
paras.pashto: د رنګ رنګ د کروموفور د شتون له امله دی او د ټینګېدو ځانګړنه یې د اسیدي یا قلوي ګروپونو لکه –OH، –SO₃H، –NH₂، –NR₂ او نورو له امله ده.

paras.urdu: قطبی آکسوکروم رنگ کو پانی میں حل پذیر بناتا ہے اور کپڑے کی ساخت کے مخالف چارج والے گروپوں سے تعامل کر کے رنگ کو کپڑے سے جوڑتا ہے۔

paras.text: Tidbit — Pigment and Dye

paras.text: Pigments and dyes are called colorants. The ways in which colorants are used determines whether they are pigments or dyes. Pigments are water and oil-insoluble, natural and synthetic products that impart colour to materials such as paper and plastics. Whereas, Dyes, are water-soluble colorants, although some are converted into insoluble lake pigments by co-precipitating onto an inorganic base. Artists’ colours are pigments that are spread on a surface suspended in a suitable medium, such as oil.

Raw materials for petrochemical industries are methane, ethane, propane and butanes. These are obtained primarily from natural gas processing plants. Gas oil and naphtha are obtained from petroleum refineries. Benzene, toluene and xylene are also primarily obtained from petroleum refineries.

Methane, benzene, toluene and xylene are used directly as feedstocks for producing petrochemicals.

Economy of Pakistan

Chemical Industry refers to the industry, which is involved in the business of making different products from raw materials through chemical reactions. Chemical sector plays a fundamental role in economic development of any nation. It converts the essential raw materials into more than seventy thousand variety products for industry as well as the goods of consumers that people depend upon their daily lives.

Pakistan trades in chemicals with other countries to earn foreign exchange in the field of chemical industry such as a fertilizer, plastics, rubber, medicine, cement, dyes and pigments soaps and detergents.

Chemical industries are very important for the economy of any country.

Chemical industries supply the farmers the pesticides and fertilizers, which are essential for crop growing. Chemical industries contribute to agriculture and food self-sufficiency of every country.

In our everyday life, we use many industrial products and most of them are related to chemical industry in some way or the other. Chemical industry produces the synthetic fibres and dyes, which are used in textile industry.

It supplies the synthetic sweeteners and synthetic flavours, which are used by food manufacturing companies.

Chemical industry indirectly helps the pharmaceutical industry and health care industry by providing the essential chemical components.

In short, chemical industry contributes indirectly to almost every sector of economy.

22.2 Safety Considerations in Process Industries

The following safety consideration in the process industry must be kept in view before launching an industrial activity.

To keep away the factory itself from corroding away, proper material construction should be selected by the designing chemical engineers.

To avoid harmful impures in raw materials, to follow the course of chemical reactions and to secure the requisite yield and purity of products, careful process control by periodic analysis is required as well as modern instrumentation and automatic control.

To transmit goods in a clean and economical manner from the manufacturer to the customer, suitable containers must be used.

To ensure the safety of workers and the plant all procedures, must be carried on in a non-hazardous manner.

To guarantee progress to continue profits and to replace obsolescent processes and equipments much attention and money must be spent upon containing research and development.

To prevent the contamination of water and air, factories must avoid discharge of toxic material into the air and water of their localities.

To label the chemicals that can help in identifying the more hazardous chemicals.

22.3 Dyes

Dyes are substances that are used to impart colour to various substrates, which adds value to products for their cost, including paper, leather, fur, hair, drugs, cosmetics, waxes, greases, plastics and textile materials.

A dye is a coloured compound, normally used in solution, which is capable of being fixed to a fabric.

The dye has a colour due to the presence of chromophore and its fixed property is due to the acidic or basic groups such as –OH, –SO₃H, –NH₂, –NR₂, etc.

The polar auxochrome makes the dye water-soluble and binds the dye to the fabric by interaction with the oppositely charged groups of fabric structure.

Properties of Dye

Dyes must possess the following four properties:

1. Colour

2. Solubility in water

3. Ability to be absorbed and retained by fibre (substantivity) or to be chemically combined with it (reactivity).

4. Ability to withstand washing, dry cleaning and exposure to light.

Tidbit — Pigment and Dye

Pigments and dyes are called colorants. The ways in which colorants are used determines whether they are pigments or dyes. Pigments are water and oil-insoluble, natural and synthetic products that impart colour to materials such as paper and plastics. Whereas, Dyes, are water-soluble colorants, although some are converted into insoluble lake pigments by co-precipitating onto an inorganic base. Artists’ colours are pigments that are spread on a surface suspended in a suitable medium, such as oil.

پیګمنټونه او رنګونه رنګوونکي (کلرنټونه) بلل کېږي. د رنګوونکو د کارولو طریقه ټاکي چې پیګمنټ دي که رنګ. پیګمنټونه په اوبو او تېلو کې نه حلېدونکي، طبیعي او مصنوعي محصولات دي چې موادو لکه کاغذ او پلاستیک ته رنګ ورکوي. په داسې حال کې چې رنګونه په اوبو کې حلېدونکي رنګوونکي دي، که څه هم ځینې یې پر یوې غیر عضوي قلوي باندې د ګډ رسوب په واسطه په نه حلېدونکو لیک پیګمنټونو بدلېږي. د هنرمندانو رنګونه هغه پیګمنټونه دي چې په یوه مناسب منځني ماده لکه تېلو کې ځړېدلي پر سطحه غوړول کېږي.

Raw materials for petrochemical industries are methane, ethane, propane and butanes. These are obtained primarily from natural gas processing plants. Gas oil and naphtha are obtained from petroleum refineries. Benzene, toluene and xylene are also primarily obtained from petroleum refineries.

Methane, benzene, toluene and xylene are used directly as feedstocks for producing petrochemicals.

Economy of Pakistan

Chemical Industry refers to the industry, which is involved in the business of making different products from raw materials through chemical reactions. Chemical sector plays a fundamental role in economic development of any nation. It converts the essential raw materials into more than seventy thousand variety products for industry as well as the goods of consumers that people depend upon their daily lives.

Pakistan trades in chemicals with other countries to earn foreign exchange in the field of chemical industry such as a fertilizer, plastics, rubber, medicine, cement, dyes and pigments soaps and detergents.

Chemical industries are very important for the economy of any country.

Chemical industries supply the farmers the pesticides and fertilizers, which are essential for crop growing. Chemical industries contribute to agriculture and food self-sufficiency of every country.

In our everyday life, we use many industrial products and most of them are related to chemical industry in some way or the other. Chemical industry produces the synthetic fibres and dyes, which are used in textile industry.

It supplies the synthetic sweeteners and synthetic flavours, which are used by food manufacturing companies.

Chemical industry indirectly helps the pharmaceutical industry and health care industry by providing the essential chemical components.

In short, chemical industry contributes indirectly to almost every sector of economy.

22.2 Safety Considerations in Process Industries

The following safety consideration in the process industry must be kept in view before launching an industrial activity.

To keep away the factory itself from corroding away, proper material construction should be selected by the designing chemical engineers.

To avoid harmful impures in raw materials, to follow the course of chemical reactions and to secure the requisite yield and purity of products, careful process control by periodic analysis is required as well as modern instrumentation and automatic control.

To transmit goods in a clean and economical manner from the manufacturer to the customer, suitable containers must be used.

To ensure the safety of workers and the plant all procedures, must be carried on in a non-hazardous manner.

To guarantee progress to continue profits and to replace obsolescent processes and equipments much attention and money must be spent upon containing research and development.

To prevent the contamination of water and air, factories must avoid discharge of toxic material into the air and water of their localities.

To label the chemicals that can help in identifying the more hazardous chemicals.

22.3 Dyes

Dyes are substances that are used to impart colour to various substrates, which adds value to products for their cost, including paper, leather, fur, hair, drugs, cosmetics, waxes, greases, plastics and textile materials.

A dye is a coloured compound, normally used in solution, which is capable of being fixed to a fabric.

The dye has a colour due to the presence of chromophore and its fixed property is due to the acidic or basic groups such as –OH, –SO₃H, –NH₂, –NR₂, etc.

The polar auxochrome makes the dye water-soluble and binds the dye to the fabric by interaction with the oppositely charged groups of fabric structure.

Properties of Dye

Dyes must possess the following four properties:

1. Colour

2. Solubility in water

3. Ability to be absorbed and retained by fibre (substantivity) or to be chemically combined with it (reactivity).

4. Ability to withstand washing, dry cleaning and exposure to light.

Tidbit — Pigment and Dye

Pigments and dyes are called colorants. The ways in which colorants are used determines whether they are pigments or dyes. Pigments are water and oil-insoluble, natural and synthetic products that impart colour to materials such as paper and plastics. Whereas, Dyes, are water-soluble colorants, although some are converted into insoluble lake pigments by co-precipitating onto an inorganic base. Artists’ colours are pigments that are spread on a surface suspended in a suitable medium, such as oil.
